design.site_summary: A damp, full shade north-facing balcony with high moisture and dripping pipes, shared with a curious cat.
design.layout_strategy: Hanging baskets with trailing foliage cascade from the upper wall, upright structural ferns and lilies sit at mid-height against the back wall, and a dense, low ground-level planting carpet covers the floor containers where the cat can safely sit.
design.combination_logic: The design combines fine-textured arching fronds with broad, glossy tropical leaves and soft, succulent trailing stems, creating a lush, jungle-like micro-landscape that thrives in perpetual shade and constant moisture.

zones.placement: On high wall hooks above eye level, full shade, north-facing, receiving constant indirect light and heavy atmospheric moisture.

plants.why: Thrives in high moisture and shade, providing a unique furry root texture that drapes over the basket edges.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes delicate, finely divided fronds and an interesting epiphytic habit that contrasts with the broader leaves below.

maintenance: Water thoroughly when the top inch of soil feels slightly damp.
Mist the fuzzy rhizomes weekly to maintain high humidity.
Trim away any yellowing or dead fronds in early spring.

zones.placement: In large containers against the north-facing back wall, full shade, sheltered from direct wind but exposed to drip zone moisture.

plants.why: Loves high moisture and shade, creating a lush green backdrop against the wall.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides massive volume and classic sword-like frond texture that fills the mid-tier effectively.

plants.why: Adapts exceptionally well to low light and consistently moist, even soggy soil conditions.
plants.role_in_combination: Offers broad, glossy, dark green leaves and occasional white blooms that contrast sharply with the fine fern foliage.

maintenance: Water every few days to keep the soil evenly moist without letting it dry out completely.
Apply a dilute liquid foliage fertilizer monthly during the growing season.
Remove spent flower stalks at the base once blooms fade in late summer.

zones.placement: In wide, heavy floor containers along the inner balcony edge, full shade, damp north exposure.

plants.why: Grows vigorously in moist shade and provides a soft, mat-forming carpet that the cat can safely interact with.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as a low, sprawling ground cover that softens the edges of the heavy floor pots and adds a creeping growth habit.

maintenance: Check moisture daily since this zone receives runoff and cat traffic.
Pin down trailing stems to encourage dense rooting.
Prune back leggy growth aggressively in mid-summer to maintain a compact carpet.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture across all containers to prevent anaerobic rot from over-watering caused by dripping pipes.
care_instructions.frequency: Twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn.

care_instructions.task: Clean accumulated dust and urban soot off the broad leaves of the Spathiphyllum and Nephrolepis using a damp cloth.
Inspect the lower floor containers for compacted soil caused by continuous dampness and cat activity, aerating gently with a hand fork.

care_cautions: Constant moisture from dripping pipes combined with heavy shade can cause waterlogging and root rot in the Upper Cascade hanging baskets if drainage holes are blocked.
The cat may over-excavate or excessively trample the low Tradescantia flumeninsis in the floor containers, requiring physical barriers or replacement cuttings.
design.pet_safety_note: The ground-level Tradescantia flumeninsis is non-toxic and provides a safe textural element for the cat to sit near and nibble, while toxic or irritating species like Dieffenbachia have been completely excluded from the plant list.
